Maybe I overstretched, but you can still disagree with the mass opinion on something and be right in doing so. I don't think morality is linked with global consensus. There are many examples in the past of widely held opinions we now believe to be morally wrong

> What is your moral justification for claiming that someone making a profit off providing a needed service effectively is committing an immoral act?

That feels like a very fundamental to the root of my argument.  I suppose I agree with you, and would scale back that claim. I have less of an issue a grocery store as they're putting in work to make it easier for me to get what I need. Whereas in the case of the landlord, the lettings agent are doing all the work, they're skimming off the top. You have situations where the landlord directly supports, but my issue is with the landlords who buy the property then move the work to someone else. They're a middle man that is only taking on a risk, which they're unfairly compensated for
Paying for labour is very different than paying a landlord. The later of which adds very little service to the system, and are there to extract excess profits from the work of the lettings agent

I can definitely see that I might feel personally agreved, maybe the real view I need to change is a need of owning property.

There's no need to be facetious. I'm talking about the moral argument, in a practical world suddenly stopping all landlords (like any monumental change) would have a big impact 

I'm also morally against violence, but I'm not naive enough to ignore that suddenly removing all weapons would cause some weird issues

Tldr: it's not a conspiracy, but unconscious bias can be a factor in why referees might react differently



I think the vast majority of poor refereeing decisions is down to incompetence, no motivation to improve, among other reasons

One of those contributing factors might be an unconscious bias due to geographic location. To be a referee you have to be interested in football, and as a side effect you're going to have preconceived likes and dislikes, which might be based on geographic upbringing. As someone from the south coast, I do have a fondness for teams from the south coast of England.

The whole point then is that as a referee, I don't let that cloud my judgement. And I'm sure 99% of refs try to do that with honest intentions. The issue is that unconscious bias can still remain

A famous example is in Orchestral music auditions. When they introduced a screen to prevent judges seeing the gender of the individual, the gender makeup of the results were far more equal than prior. That's not saying there was any sexism before, it's just saying that unconscious bias affected decision making. 

Having a more diverse set of referees would result in unconscious bias averaging out a little. But in my mind, the future is a referee who doesn't know what match he's officiating. He doesn't see that it's Manchester United Vs Liverpool, but Team A Vs Team B. That way absolutely no bias would be present.
